scope_review: The learner drives or prepares a normal passenger car; no specialist vehicle operating rules.
learning_objective: Calculate distance travelled before braking during reaction time
novelty_review: Existing speed questions concern limits and adapting speed; none asks the distance travelled during an explicitly specified reaction time. Exact calculation is 90 / 3.6 = 25 m/s.

fr.question_text: À 90 km/h, avec un temps de réaction d’une seconde, quelle distance est parcourue avant le début du freinage ?
fr.explanation: 90 km/h correspondent à 25 mètres par seconde. Pendant une seconde de réaction, la voiture parcourt donc environ 25 mètres avant que le freinage commence. La distance de freinage s’ajoute ensuite.

en.question_text: At 90 km/h, with a reaction time of one second, how far does the car travel before braking begins?
en.explanation: 90 km/h equals 25 metres per second. During a one-second reaction time, the car therefore travels about 25 metres before braking begins. The braking distance must then be added.

visual_review: Reviewed blue car brake lamps on a dry divided road with visible gap; no misleading speed readout or distance annotation. Question explicitly supplies 90 km/h and one second; independently calculated 90/3.6=25. C uniquely correct; reaction and braking distances distinguished in FR/EN.
